cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Nobody came to the moot. That's never happened. They didn't come because they've decided, and they don't need a moot to tell them. I came, because someone should tell you.

left.label: Ask what they decided
left.outcome: "That you're the Company's. That the Company's the flood. Work it out."

right.label: The moot is not my concern
right.outcome: "No. It'll be at your door, though. It'll bring lamps."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. The hands won't take orders from the Keeper's mouth, only from mine. The town's stopped selling the lock house bread. And somebody's cut the tow rope on the Company boat. Clean.

left.label: Give orders through Dace
left.outcome: The gate runs on Dace's word. He does not enjoy it as much as you'd think.

right.label: The Keeper gives the orders
right.outcome: Orders are given. Some are obeyed. Slowly.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The town is angry with you, and angry towns pay late. I am owed by half of it. If the Keeper would like the town calmer, the Keeper could pay its debts to me. I would announce who paid. Kindly.

left.label: Pay the town's debts to Cole
left.outcome: You are, briefly, the most popular person in Halfway. Cole is the richest.

right.label: The town's debts are the town's
right.outcome: "Of course. Then it will remain angry, and I shall remain patient."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: Someone has put a dead rat on the Keeper's step. Then another. Rats carry things, and the person doing it is a patient of mine. I will not say who. Stop giving them reasons.

left.label: Ask what reasons
left.outcome: "The Company's. Every day you do its work in its voice, the town hears it."

right.label: Find who did it
right.outcome: Dace finds him. It is Perrin. He has four children and a flooded cellar.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A child throws a stone at the Keeper's window and runs. The stone has a paper round it. The paper says GO HOME in a careful adult hand that has been to the town school.

left.label: Post the paper on the gate
left.outcome: The town reads its own handwriting. Some are ashamed. Some sign it.

right.label: Burn it; mend the window
right.outcome: Tamm mends the window and says nothing, which is a kindness.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: The town wants you gone. That's a story. 'KEEPER BESIEGED', or 'TOWN TURNS ON ITS OWN KEEPER'. Victim or villain? I've got type for both.

left.label: 'Besieged'
left.outcome: Sorrel pities you. The town hates being pitied more than it hates you.

right.label: Neither; print the water figures
right.outcome: He prints them. The town reads them. Something shifts, not toward you, but away from the Company.

cards.speaker: tobin
cards.text: They ran a Keeper out in my day. Year 44. Walked him to the stone with lamps, quiet as a funeral. He'd done nothing much, for too long. You've done more. Might not help.

left.label: Ask what would have helped him
left.outcome: "One thing they could see. One. Didn't have to be big."

right.label: Buy him a drink and say nothing
right.outcome: He drinks it. "Dray sat there too. Same face."

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: They're saying things about you at the inn. The things they said about him, before. I told them to stop. They told me I live in your house. I do. I'm asking if I should keep living in it.

left.label: Stay; it is your house
left.outcome: "It is." She stays. The inn talks about that too.

right.label: Go to Ilse's until this passes
right.outcome: She goes. The house is very quiet. The town approves of her, at least.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The moot met without me and voted to withhold the town's labor from the gate. No hands but the Company's. No repairs. No sandbags. I'm telling you as reeve. As Ilse, I'd have voted the same.

left.label: Requisition labor under the emergency clause
left.outcome: You compel the town. It comes, and it does not forget the compelling.

right.label: Work with the Company's hands alone
right.outcome: Dace and four men run a summit lock. The gate slows to a crawl.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. The hands have been asked, by the town, to walk out. Half want to. And the half that don't have asked me to ask you for one reason to stay that isn't wages.

left.label: 'Someone must watch the water'
left.outcome: Dace repeats it. It is not what they expected. They stay.

right.label: Wages are the reason
right.outcome: "Right." Half walk out. The other half work double.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: If the town runs you out, the Keeper's house falls to me under the default clause. I would rather it did not. I am telling you so you know my interest is honest.

left.label: Ask her to speak at the moot
left.outcome: Cole speaks. The town listens to money. It buys a month.

right.label: Your interest is noted
right.outcome: "Kindly. I shall have the locks measured, just in case."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: A man came to me with a broken hand from hitting the Company house door at night. Drunk and ashamed. He was not alone. There were eleven. I am telling you the number.

left.label: Open the Company house to the town
left.outcome: You hold a meeting in the Company's own parlor. Pell is appalled. The town is astonished.

right.label: Bar the door and post a guard
right.outcome: Dace's man on the step all night. Eleven becomes twenty.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: The town has painted the boundary stone white and cleared the path to it. Nobody has said why. Everybody knows why. A child asks you, quite kindly, whether you will need a lamp for the walk.

left.label: 'I hope not'
left.outcome: The child considers this and offers to lend you one anyway.

right.label: Have the stone repainted grey
right.outcome: It is white again by morning.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: There's a petition going round for your removal. A hundred names. I've seen it. Half of them are in the same hand and that hand is Cole's clerk. I could print that. It would be very funny and very cruel.

left.label: Print it
left.outcome: The petition dies laughing. Cole does not speak to you for a month.

right.label: Leave the petition alone
right.outcome: "Merciful. Wasted, but merciful." A hundred names reach Ardent.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: I've held them off a month. I can't hold them another. They want the Keeper at the moot tonight, to answer for the Company. Come, and they might not walk you out. I'm promising nothing.

left.label: Go to the moot
left.outcome: Three hours of shouting. At the end, nobody walks anywhere. It is not forgiveness. It is a start.

right.label: The Keeper does not answer to moots
right.outcome: "Then get your lamp."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: They've started calling it 'the Keeper's gate' at the inn. Not the Company's. Yours. It's meant kindly. I've been reeve long enough to know what kindly turns into when the Company hears it.

left.label: Let them call it what they like
left.outcome: The name sticks. Vosk hears it. She writes it down.

right.label: It is the Company's gate
right.outcome: "Say it at the inn, then. Loud. They need reminding, for their own good."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: The hands have made you a sign for the gate. It says KEEPER'S LOCK. They want to hang it over the Company's. And Pell's coming Thursday.

left.label: Hang it
left.outcome: KEEPER'S LOCK over MERIDIAN CANAL COMPANY. Pell sees it Thursday and goes a color.

right.label: Hang it in the lock house, inside
right.outcome: Inside. The hands are pleased anyway. Pell never sees it.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The town loves you. I have watched towns love people; it is expensive. They will ask for things and remember every refusal. I would like to be your first refusal. I am asking for nothing.

left.label: Then you have it
left.outcome: "Kindly. Now everyone else knows you can say no. You owe me."

right.label: I will refuse when I must
right.outcome: "Everyone says that. Everyone is wrong. Kindly."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: You are the most popular Keeper in eighty years and you look worse than any of them. Popularity is a symptom. The town wants you at every bedside, every wedding, every moot. Stop going to some of them.

left.label: Stop going to some
left.outcome: You miss a wedding. The couple forgives you. You sleep.

right.label: The town needs its Keeper
right.outcome: "Its Keeper needs a liver. I am a physician, not a friend, but I am also that."

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A deputation from the town: they would like the Keeper to stand for reeve. Ilse has said she'd step aside. The Company forbids Keepers from holding town office. The Company has not been asked.

left.label: Stand
left.outcome: You are reeve and Keeper. The Company learns from the Courier.

right.label: Ilse is the reeve
right.outcome: The deputation goes away pleased anyway. Ilse is quietly relieved.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: THE TOWN THAT LOVES ITS KEEPER. It's a lovely piece. It's also the kind of piece that gets read in Ardent as THE KEEPER WHO LOVES THE TOWN, which is a different piece. Shall I run it?

left.label: Run it
left.outcome: The town frames it. Ardent files it under something else.

right.label: Run something about the water instead
right.outcome: He runs the gauge figures with no headline. It is the quietest thing he has ever printed. Ardent notices anyway.

cards.speaker: tobin
cards.text: They loved a Keeper once, in Year 44. Rose for him when the Company crossed him. Company hanged three men for it. Him they sent east. Love's a thing to be careful with.

left.label: Ask what he'd have done
left.outcome: "Told them to sit down before they stood up. He didn't. He liked being loved."

right.label: The town can stand if it likes
right.outcome: "It can. It'll stand on you."

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: They like you. The town. They didn't like him; they respected him, which is different. I don't know which is better. I know which one they'd fight for. Would you let them?

left.label: Never
left.outcome: "Good. He'd have said that." She almost smiles.

right.label: If it came to it
right.outcome: "Then it will. Things do, here."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The moot voted last night. Not about you. For you. They've voted the town won't obey any Company order the Keeper hasn't signed. I said that's sedition. They said it's loyalty. It's both.

left.label: Ask them to rescind it
left.outcome: They rescind, sulking. Ardent never hears. You breathe.

right.label: Let it stand
right.outcome: It stands. Fennick wires it to Ardent before you can stop him. He thought you'd be pleased.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. A Company inspector came to count the hands and the hands wouldn't be counted without the Keeper present. He left. Ardent's wired. And the hands think it was funny.

left.label: Be present for the recount
left.outcome: You stand there while a small man counts eleven people. Nobody laughs. Nearly.

right.label: It was funny
right.outcome: "It was." Ardent does not think so.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: Tenants are refusing rent 'until the Keeper says'. I have never needed a Keeper's leave to collect rent. I am asking politely. I have other ways of asking.

left.label: Tell them to pay
left.outcome: They pay. They also learn you and Cole are on the same side, which you are not.

right.label: The rent is between you and them
right.outcome: "Then the buildings are between me and the Company. Kindly."

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: Men at the inn last night were talking about the Company house and what burns. I did not think they meant it in Year 44 either. You are the only one they will listen to.

left.label: Go to the inn tonight and speak
left.outcome: You speak. They listen, sullenly, and put down whatever they were holding.

right.label: Send Dace
right.outcome: Dace goes. He is one of them. He comes back quiet.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A crowd at the gate, cheerful, with a barrel. They have come to carry the Keeper shoulder-high round the town for no reason anyone can give. The Company house windows are all lit and all watching.

left.label: Be carried
left.outcome: Round the town twice. Vosk, at her window, does not close the curtain.

right.label: Stand them a drink instead
right.outcome: They drink. They carry Dace instead, who hates it.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: My son died the week after the town rose for a Keeper. I've never told you that. I'm telling you because the town's about to do it again and I'd rather bury you than another boy. Stop them.

left.label: Stop them
left.outcome: You stand on the wharf and tell the town to go home. It does, for you. Only for you.

right.label: I cannot stop them
right.outcome: "You can. You won't. It's the same thing when there's a lamp in the window."

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: Ardent has a word for a post whose town obeys the Keeper over the Company: sedition. It's in a wire I've seen, with your name in it. I'd like to print it. You'd like me not to.

left.label: Print it
left.outcome: The town reads that it is seditious and is delighted. Ardent is not.

right.label: Hold it
right.outcome: "Held. For now. I hold things about a month."
